answer.short:
$$f(x)=\frac{(f(x)+g(x))+(f(x)-g(x))}{2}.$$

The black sketch lies midway vertically between the supplied coloured curves. It passes through their common negative-$x$ intercept.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}(f(x)+g(x))+(f(x)-g(x))&=2f(x),\\f(x)&=\frac{(f(x)+g(x))+(f(x)-g(x))}{2}.\end{align*}$$

At each common $x$-value, average the ordinates of the coloured curves. This places $f$ halfway vertically between them. Where both supplied curves meet the $x$-axis, their average is zero, so the graph of $f$ passes through that same point. Swapping the two coloured curves does not change their average.

The black curve below is the graphical midpoint of the two supplied curves over their displayed extent. Keep their common negative-$x$ intercept. No numerical scale or formula for the supplied curves is given.
